pathway.title: Chord Energy Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity and maturities are the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 2,774.4 million combines cash with USD 1,969.7 million of undrawn revolver commitments, the two notes of USD 750.0 million each fall due in 2030 and 2033 at fixed rates, and the revolver now matures in 2031; with nothing due for almost four years, refinancing risk is low and the revolver is a second line behind cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation K3

Reported leverage is low and the fall since FY2025 is real: net debt over EBITDA was 0.22x at 2026-09-30 against 0.77x at FY2025 and 0.36x at FY2024, and 0.58x at FY2025 even after adding back the non-cash impairment. After USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04 it is 0.25x; the pro forma effect of the Marcellus Shale sale is not established because closing and net proceeds are not stated. EBITDA is derived, not issuer-stated, and excludes hedge settlements. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K4

Cash generation is strong at today's prices and entirely price-dependent. Free cash flow was USD 1,307.73 million in nine months 2026, 49.82% of EBITDA, because the average crude sales price was USD 83.54 per Bbl against USD 64.73 a year earlier and USD 62.78 in FY2025. Hedges cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes but only 24.63% of last-twelve-months volumes for 2027 (31.15% with contracts added after the quarter), so most of the price exposure is open. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation K6; calculation H1; calculation H2; calculation H3

Business quality is average to strong on scale and cost control and weak on diversification. Crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, Phillips 66 and Marathon Petroleum Supply & Trading took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales, and 89% of reserves are operated on acreage that is almost all held by production, which lets Chord pace spending; lease operating expense per Boe rose to USD 10.24 in nine months 2026 from USD 9.74, so unit costs are drifting up. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Financial policy is the main discretionary risk. Distributions equalled 106.10% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 98.54% in FY2025 before falling to 48.77% in nine months 2026, and net debt rose USD 484.4 million in 2025 as acquisitions were paid with notes and cash; with no sponsor to extract value, the exposure is a payout policy that tiers up as leverage falls, which would use the cash cushion that currently supports the credit. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

Covenant headroom and legal capacity cannot be assessed. The revolver carries a leverage test below 3.50x and a current ratio test of at least 1.0x, compliance is stated without figures, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so strong liquidity is a statement about cash and undrawn commitments, not about what lenders could restrict. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity: USD 2,774.4 million of cash and undrawn commitments sit against no debt maturity until 2030, so a downturn would have to last years to threaten debt service, and the amended revolver extends the second line to 2031. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

The second strength is low reported leverage with high interest cover: net debt over EBITDA of 0.22x (0.25x after USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04) and EBITDA covering interest expense 28.88x leave a wide cushion before debt service is pressured, although the cover is built on derived EBITDA at a high oil price. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K5

The third strength is operator control: 89% of reserves are operated and the acreage is almost all held by production, so Chord can cut capital spending in a downturn instead of losing most leases, which protects free cash flow when prices fall, although the annual report warns that some undeveloped leases expire unless drilled. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19

The fourth strength is the hedge book: collars and swaps cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes, which sets a floor under near-term cash flow while leaving upside above the ceilings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation H1

The fifth strength is refinancing capacity: the 2025 issue of USD 750.0 million of notes due 2033 replaced notes due 2026 with unsecured debt and the revolver was extended twice, so lender appetite and market access were shown in 2025. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

The first weakness is price dependence and concentration: crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, so EBITDA moves with the oil price almost one for one, and a fall of 18.61% in the crude price would cut last-twelve-months EBITDA by 27.26%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P4

The second weakness is payout policy: distributions equalled 98.54% of FY2025 free cash flow, so little cash was left for debt reduction in a year when net debt rose USD 484.4 million, and the policy tiers up as leverage falls. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

The third weakness is customer and takeaway concentration: two purchasers took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales and the annual report names reliance on a limited number of midstream providers and a possible Dakota Access Pipeline shutdown, either of which would cut volumes or widen differentials. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178

The fourth weakness is the unsupplied legal framework: two amendments raised baskets and thresholds without terms being supplied, so the capacity for distributions, new debt and liens is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

The fifth weakness is event risk: the company has grown through three combinations since 2022, a Marcellus Shale sale is pending, and the signing chief executive changed without explanation, so strategy and leverage could shift quickly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Chord's transactions follow a consistent pattern of buying scale with stock, cash and notes and then pruning. The Enerplus combination in May 2024 paid USD 375.8 million in cash and issued shares, and the XTO assets bought in October 2025 cost USD 540.4 million, funded by the 2030 notes and cash. The company issued two series of senior unsecured notes in 2025, USD 750.0 million due 2033 in March and USD 750.0 million due 2030 in September, using the first to repurchase and discharge the 2026 notes and the second to fund the XTO purchase. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165

Two events after the September 2026 balance sheet date bear on creditors. The Eighth Amendment of 2026-10-30 extended the revolver to 2031 and raised thresholds, and the pending Marcellus Shale sale of USD 550.0 million is expected to close in the fourth quarter. Neither the amendment's terms nor the sale's net proceeds are stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chord's reported balance sheet is lightly levered and the fall in leverage over 2026 is real, so creditors hold thick earnings cover over debt that matures no earlier than 2030. Net debt was 0.22x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 0.77x at FY2025 and 0.36x at FY2024, with USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity.

fields.value: Chord Energy Corp (chrd-1486159), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway: Business & governance from the two annual reports and three quarterly reports supplied, through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. It covers the business, ownership and control, operating model, issuer history and governance behaviour, and draws no ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chord is a scaled, single-basin oil producer with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so creditors face concentration and capital-return risk, not extraction risk, and governance risk is medium. Distributions took 106.10% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 98.54% in FY2025, then 48.77% in nine months 2026.

fields.value: The pattern that matters is debt-funded acquisition followed by a cash build as higher oil prices lifted cash flow: net debt rose USD 484.4 million during 2025 and the Marcellus Shale sale for USD 550.0 million is pending. The credit agreement is unsupplied and the signing chief executive changed without explanation, so capacity and continuity are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is large and concentrated, which gives creditors scale but little diversification. Chord operates almost entirely in one basin with one reportable segment, crude oil is 91.73% of oil, NGL and gas revenues and 56% of proved reserves, and the company operates 89% of its reserves on acreage that is almost all held by production, so it can pace capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and takeaway concentration are the operating dependencies that matter most to cash flow. Phillips 66 took 21% and Marathon Petroleum Supply & Trading 12% of FY2025 product sales, and the annual report names a limited number of midstream providers and a possible Dakota Access Pipeline shutdown as risks; an outage would force shut-ins or wider price differentials and cut cash flow, although management says other purchasers exist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, and no extraction behaviour is documented, but shareholder returns are policy-driven and were large against free cash flow. The board is 82% independent, the variable dividend was dropped after 2024, and the share count fell 10.81% between February 2025 and October 2026, yet returns equalled 98.54% of FY2025 free cash flow, leaving no deleveraging cushion in a year of debt-funded acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Chord presents medium governance risk. The supported behaviour is large, cash-flow-funded shareholder returns with a falling share count, which matters because distributions near free cash flow leave little room to absorb a price fall or a debt-funded deal, and implies that creditor protection rests on leverage staying low rather than on structural restraint. Countervailing evidence is a base-only dividend, a declining payout share in 2026 and no documented creditor-adverse action.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a benign reading is that no sponsor exists, no liability-management or priming action is documented, the 2025 refinancing replaced notes with longer unsecured notes, and 2026 returns used under half of free cash flow with no new debt. The view would turn adverse if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or a new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, if a debt-funded acquisition followed the XTO deal, or if the unsupplied credit agreement shows wide capacity for restricted payments after the amendments. It would improve if a compliance certificate and the agreements show tight restricted-payment limits, or if the explanation of the chief executive change shows continuity of the capital-return policy.

fields.value: Chord Energy Corp (chrd-1486159), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway: Fundamental credit synthesis of business quality, financial profile, outlook and downside from the five filings and the three earlier analyses. It assigns no rating, draws no legal-capacity conclusion and sizes no position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chord's fundamentals are strong on liquidity, maturities and reported leverage but depend on an oil price well above 2025's, so a price fall would reach creditors through cash and distributions long before it threatened debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 0.22x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 0.25x after USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04, with USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity and no maturity before the 2030 notes. At the FY2025 average crude price, 18.61% below the last-twelve-months average of USD 77.13 per Bbl, net leverage would be 0.30x and distributions 1.26x free cash flow, a gap that cash would cover for 5.35 years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 2,774.4 million combines cash with USD 1,969.7 million of undrawn revolver commitments, the two notes of USD 750.0 million each fall due in 2030 and 2033 at fixed rates, and the revolver now matures in 2031; with nothing due for almost four years, refinancing risk is low and the revolver is a second line behind cash.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation K3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is low and the fall since FY2025 is real: net debt over EBITDA was 0.22x at 2026-09-30 against 0.77x at FY2025 and 0.36x at FY2024, and 0.58x at FY2025 even after adding back the non-cash impairment. After USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04 it is 0.25x; the pro forma effect of the Marcellus Shale sale is not established because closing and net proceeds are not stated. EBITDA is derived, not issuer-stated, and excludes hedge settlements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong at today's prices and entirely price-dependent. Free cash flow was USD 1,307.73 million in nine months 2026, 49.82% of EBITDA, because the average crude sales price was USD 83.54 per Bbl against USD 64.73 a year earlier and USD 62.78 in FY2025. Hedges cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes but only 24.63% of last-twelve-months volumes for 2027 (31.15% with contracts added after the quarter), so most of the price exposure is open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation K6; calculation H1; calculation H2; calculation H3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business quality is average to strong on scale and cost control and weak on diversification. Crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, Phillips 66 and Marathon Petroleum Supply & Trading took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales, and 89% of reserves are operated on acreage that is almost all held by production, which lets Chord pace spending; lease operating expense per Boe rose to USD 10.24 in nine months 2026 from USD 9.74, so unit costs are drifting up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main discretionary risk. Distributions equalled 106.10% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 98.54% in FY2025 before falling to 48.77% in nine months 2026, and net debt rose USD 484.4 million in 2025 as acquisitions were paid with notes and cash; with no sponsor to extract value, the exposure is a payout policy that tiers up as leverage falls, which would use the cash cushion that currently supports the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom and legal capacity cannot be assessed. The revolver carries a leverage test below 3.50x and a current ratio test of at least 1.0x, compliance is stated without figures, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so strong liquidity is a statement about cash and undrawn commitments, not about what lenders could restrict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a strong reading is that FY2025 net profit was close to nil after the impairment with gross leverage of 0.89x, and that the 2026 recovery came with an oil price that management links to the Middle East conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The view would weaken if the crude sales price fell back to the FY2025 level while buybacks continued, if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, or if the unsupplied covenant terms are tighter than the headline liquidity implies. It would strengthen if hedge cover for 2027 rose well above a quarter of volumes at floors near USD 65.54 per Bbl, if buybacks were kept below free cash flow, or if a compliance certificate showed wide headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario applies one price anchor to last-twelve-months volumes and leaves out hedge settlements and lower production taxes, so it overstates the near-term shortfall and understates exposure beyond the hedge horizon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant ratios and the definitions behind them are not printed, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions treat lender tests as untested, and headroom could be thinner than liquidity alone suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No production, price or cost guidance after February 2026 is supplied, so the twelve to twenty-four month outlook rests on reported run-rates and hedges rather than on management's plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating or dated market price is supplied, so the market-access conclusion relies on the 2025 note issuance and not on where the notes trade.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity: USD 2,774.4 million of cash and undrawn commitments sit against no debt maturity until 2030, so a downturn would have to last years to threaten debt service, and the amended revolver extends the second line to 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is low reported leverage with high interest cover: net debt over EBITDA of 0.22x (0.25x after USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04) and EBITDA covering interest expense 28.88x leave a wide cushion before debt service is pressured, although the cover is built on derived EBITDA at a high oil price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is operator control: 89% of reserves are operated and the acreage is almost all held by production, so Chord can cut capital spending in a downturn instead of losing most leases, which protects free cash flow when prices fall, although the annual report warns that some undeveloped leases expire unless drilled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is the hedge book: collars and swaps cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes, which sets a floor under near-term cash flow while leaving upside above the ceilings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is refinancing capacity: the 2025 issue of USD 750.0 million of notes due 2033 replaced notes due 2026 with unsecured debt and the revolver was extended twice, so lender appetite and market access were shown in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is price dependence and concentration: crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, so EBITDA moves with the oil price almost one for one, and a fall of 18.61% in the crude price would cut last-twelve-months EBITDA by 27.26%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is payout policy: distributions equalled 98.54% of FY2025 free cash flow, so little cash was left for debt reduction in a year when net debt rose USD 484.4 million, and the policy tiers up as leverage falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is customer and takeaway concentration: two purchasers took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales and the annual report names reliance on a limited number of midstream providers and a possible Dakota Access Pipeline shutdown, either of which would cut volumes or widen differentials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is the unsupplied legal framework: two amendments raised baskets and thresholds without terms being supplied, so the capacity for distributions, new debt and liens is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is event risk: the company has grown through three combinations since 2022, a Marcellus Shale sale is pending, and the signing chief executive changed without explanation, so strategy and leverage could shift quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chord is an independent oil and gas producer whose cash flow comes from crude oil sold to refiners and marketers from the Williston Basin, with a limited non-operated gas interest in the Marcellus Shale that is held for sale. It operates most of its portfolio, markets its own production, and has been built through the Whiting merger of 2022, the Enerplus combination of 2024 and the XTO purchase of 2025; the single basin and single product give cash-flow visibility only to the extent hedges and the oil price allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chord is widely held, with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the credit does not carry sponsor extraction risk but also has no committed support. The borrower under the revolver is a subsidiary and certain subsidiaries guarantee the revolver and both notes, but the guarantors are not named, so structural priority cannot be assessed here; the business and governance review rates governance risk as medium because distributions have run near free cash flow and the credit agreement is unsupplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is price-driven and not contractually recurring. Production revenue rose with the crude sales price from USD 64.73 to USD 83.54 per Bbl between nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, while the quarterly price fell 8.71% from the second to the third quarter of 2026, which shows the volatility that creditors carry. Chord is a price taker; its levers are volume and marketing, and purchased oil and gas sales add revenue at close to nil margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended at current prices but the cost trend is adverse. Lease operating expense per Boe rose from USD 9.74 to USD 10.24 and the production tax rate from 7.4% to 8.1% of oil, NGL and gas revenues, so costs absorb a share of any price gain; EBITDA margin on total revenues was 45.96% on the last twelve months against 34.19% in FY2025, a swing that is mostly price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation K9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts to free cash flow at about half in nine months 2026 and at 41.54% in FY2025, so capital spending absorbs roughly half of EBITDA. The planned 2026 capital programme of USD 1.35 billion to USD 1.45 billion is largely discretionary on held-by-production acreage, which gives Chord the lever to protect free cash flow if prices fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; calculation K6; calculation K9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry and substitutes matter through price: Chord is a price taker in a commodity market, and energy-transition and supply decisions by other producers set the price that drives cash flow. Buyer power is concentrated but limited on price because realised prices follow NYMEX WTI and other purchasers exist, while supplier power shows in service-cost inflation and in a limited set of midstream providers; new entrants are unlikely to match the acreage position quickly, an Analyst Judgement that supports Chord's standing without changing price exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and economic factors are the material categories. Geopolitical disruption raised oil prices in 2026, and a change in OPEC+ policy, including a member leaving the group in May 2026, could reverse them; tribal and federal regulation on the Fort Berthold Reservation and a title dispute with the MHA Nation add a regulatory and legal exposure whose size is not stated. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the materials supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are liquidity, low reported leverage and operator control; weaknesses are price dependence, payout policy and concentration. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Marcellus Shale proceeds used to retain cash and a longer hedge book; threats are a price fall toward the FY2025 level, a pipeline outage and a debt-funded acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions the profile reads strong for scale, liquidity and ability to refinance, average for competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability and financial policy, and weak for diversification. Margin and free cash flow stability are rated average rather than strong because FY2025 EBITDA was only 54.05% of the last-twelve-months level; liquidity is strong on USD 2,774.4 million; refinancing is strong on no maturity before 2030 though no rating or market price is supplied; financial policy is average with medium governance risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but price-contingent. Tailwinds are the higher oil price, improved Williston Basin takeaway, a hedge floor on 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 volumes and the Marcellus Shale proceeds; headwinds are cost inflation, a rate rise in the third quarter of 2026 that tightens financial conditions, geopolitical reversal and the open 2027 hedge book. Over three to five years the question is whether payout policy and acquisitions keep leverage near its present level, which neither company guidance nor a rating in the sources settles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation H1; calculation H2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a return of the crude price to the FY2025 average of USD 62.78 per Bbl, 18.61% below the last-twelve-months average of USD 77.13 per Bbl, while distributions continue. On last-twelve-months volumes that price would cut revenue and EBITDA by the same amount, leaving EBITDA at 72.74% of its reported level and net leverage at 0.30x, or 0.34x after the buybacks to 2026-11-04; free cash flow would fall to 79.08% of distributions, so distributions would run at 1.26x free cash flow, although the annualised base dividend alone would still be covered. The break comes in cash, not in debt service: cash would cover 5.35 years of that shortfall, buybacks of USD 529.0 million capacity could be stopped, capital spending could be cut, and no maturity falls due before 2030. This is an Analyst Judgement anchored to the reported FY2025 price; it omits hedge settlements and lower production taxes, so it overstates the near-term shortfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Chord presents a strong liquidity and refinancing position and an adequate business profile, supported by low reported leverage, USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity and operator control, but credit quality is constrained by price dependence, a payout policy that has run near free cash flow and an unsupplied legal framework. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: strong at the current price and contingent on hedges and spending cuts if prices fall. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the oil price and on whether distributions stay below free cash flow, since nothing matures before 2030. The primary downside path is a crude price fall that turns free cash flow below distributions and draws down cash. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, covenant figures, an agency view and 2027 guidance.
